name: Tempester Voice 1.5.1.0 — the first Tempester Voice OS
summary: DSI Voice 1.5 with a hardened parser (no more permanent mute), a full command queue test, traps that reset, a checked calibration page, release times up to 60 s, the Note FX state reset by a new burst and its own version reply (0xFE00: 0x16).

fixes: A voice no longer goes silent for good when a sound message is cut short: the chip finds its place again within a few milliseconds.
A stray calibration command can no longer mute a voice: the chip calibrates only when the Main really asks for it.
A full message queue no longer looks empty and throws away a whole sound: only a message that arrives when it is full is dropped.
A voice that hits an internal error restarts by itself and keeps its voice number, instead of staying stuck.
A half-written tuning page is no longer used: the voice falls back to its default tuning, as when no page was ever saved.
A note that follows a cut-off Note FX note no longer plays with the previous sound's settings.
A full backup stays in step with the voice chips when the Main restarts on its own.
additions: Release times above 100 rise smoothly up to 60 seconds at 127; 0 to 100 sound exactly as before, and 124 to 127 no longer hold forever.
Each chip reports its own version (Voice 1.6 on the System screen), so Tempester 1.6.7.0 and later can lift the Release limit to 127.

description: Installed on the six chips on 14/11/2026 and verified by a full backup (pages 0-40 of each chip equal to this image); proved on the simulator before. Superseded by 1.5.1.1 (the same fixes, and its dump stream wraps at the end of the flash): no longer offered for building or sending (author, 15/11/2026); kept for its history row and to name what a chip holds. Recipes patch/voice/*.json, each assembled from its own source, proved on the Voice simulator. Installed on the six chips at once over MIDI (update 72 broadcasts), with a full backup 44 (Main 1.6.6.0) right before and right after; no PICkit prerequisite (author, 13/11/2026).
